title.zh: 卷七十七 志第五十三 食貨一
title.raw: 卷七十七 志第五十三 食貨一 Volume 77 Treatises 53: Finance and Economics 1

sentences.zh: 《記》曰：「取財於地，而取法於天。

translations.literal: The Classic says: "Obtain wealth from the earth, and take governance as a model from Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The Classic says: "Draw wealth from the land, and take your standards from Heaven."

sentences.zh: 富國之本，在於農桑。

translations.literal: The foundation of enriching the state lies in agriculture and sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: The foundation of a prosperous state is agriculture and sericulture.

sentences.zh: 」明初，沿元之舊，錢法不通而用鈔，又禁民間以銀交易，宜若不便於民。

translations.literal: " In the early Ming, following Yuan practice, coinage was not circulated and paper notes were used instead; moreover, private transactions in silver were forbidden — this would seem to have been inconvenient for the people.
translations.idiomatic: " In the early Ming, the dynasty retained Yuan currency practices: coin did not circulate and paper notes were used instead, while private trade in silver was forbidden — conditions that would seem plainly burdensome for ordinary people.

sentences.zh: 而洪、永、熙、宣之際，百姓充實，府藏衍溢。

translations.literal: Yet during the reigns of Hongwu, Yongle, Hongxi, and Xuande, the common people were abundantly provided for and the government treasuries overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet under Hongwu, Yongle, Hongxi, and Xuande, the people were well provided for and the state coffers overflowed.

sentences.zh: 蓋是時，劭農務墾闢，土無萊蕪，人敦本業，又開屯田、中鹽以給邊軍，餫餉不仰藉於縣官，故上下交足，軍民胥裕。

translations.literal: This was because at that time agriculture was vigorously promoted and wasteland was reclaimed; no land lay fallow, and people devoted themselves to their primary occupations. Further, military colonies and salt-monopoly transport were opened to supply the frontier armies, so that grain rations did not depend on the county officials. Thus both upper and lower levels were fully supplied, and soldiers and civilians alike were prospering.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the state vigorously promoted farming and land reclamation; fields lay uncultivated nowhere, and people kept to their primary occupations. Military colonies and salt-transport schemes supplied the frontier armies, so that grain rations no longer depended on county officials. Both court and countryside were fully supplied, and soldiers and civilians alike prospered.

sentences.zh: 其後，屯田壞於豪強之兼併，計臣變鹽法。

translations.literal: Later, military colonies were ruined by the encroachments of powerful local magnates, and fiscal planners altered the salt laws.
translations.idiomatic: Later, military colonies were ruined by encroachment from powerful local magnates, and fiscal officials rewrote the salt laws.

sentences.zh: 於是邊兵悉仰食太倉，轉輸住往不給。

translations.literal: Consequently the frontier troops all depended on grain from the Grand Granary, and transport supply frequently fell short.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier troops then came to depend entirely on grain from the Grand Granary, and transport supply often failed to keep pace.

sentences.zh: 世宗以後，耗財之道廣，府庫匱竭。

translations.literal: After the Shizong reign, the avenues of expenditure multiplied and the treasuries were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jiajing Emperor, channels of expenditure multiplied and the treasuries were drained.

sentences.zh: 神宗乃加賦重徵，礦稅四出，移正供以實左藏。

translations.literal: The Shenzong Emperor then imposed additional taxes and heavy levies, sent mining taxes everywhere, and diverted regular tribute to fill the Left Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The Wanli Emperor responded with supplemental levies and heavier taxation, dispatched mining taxes in every direction, and diverted regular tribute revenue to fill the Left Treasury.

sentences.zh: 中涓羣小，橫斂侵漁。

translations.literal: Eunuch attendants and petty men extorted and plundered at will.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch attendants and petty officials extorted and plundered at will.

sentences.zh: 民多逐末，田卒汙萊。

translations.literal: The people largely turned to secondary pursuits, and fields ultimately lay abandoned and overgrown.
translations.idiomatic: The people turned increasingly to trade and secondary pursuits, and fields were left to run wild.

sentences.zh: 吏不能拊循，而覆侵刻之。

translations.literal: Officials could not comfort and guide them, but instead compounded their oppression and exactions.
translations.idiomatic: Officials failed to comfort and guide them, and instead added further oppression and exactions.

sentences.zh: 海內困敝，而儲積益以空乏。

translations.literal: The realm within the seas grew weary and impoverished, while stored reserves became increasingly depleted.
translations.idiomatic: The empire grew exhausted and impoverished, while stored reserves dwindled ever further.

sentences.zh: 昧者多言復通鈔法可以富國，不知國初之充裕在勤農桑，而不在行鈔法也。

translations.literal: The uninformed often asserted that reviving the paper-note system could enrich the state, not knowing that the abundance of the dynasty's founding lay in diligent cultivation of agriculture and sericulture, and not in the circulation of paper notes.
translations.idiomatic: The uninformed often claimed that reviving paper currency would enrich the state, not understanding that the dynasty's early abundance came from diligent farming and sericulture, not from the circulation of paper notes.

sentences.zh: 夫韁本節用，為理財之要。

translations.literal: Holding fast to fundamentals and economizing on expenditures are the essentials of managing state finances.
translations.idiomatic: Strengthening the economic foundation and restraining expenditure are the essentials of fiscal management.

sentences.zh: 明一代理財之道，始所以得，終所以失，條其本末，著於篇。

translations.literal: The methods of managing finances throughout the Ming dynasty — how they were initially gained and ultimately lost — are here set forth in sequence, root and branch, in this treatise.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming dynasty's fiscal methods — how they were first established and how they were ultimately lost — are here traced from root to branch in this chapter.

sentences.zh: ○戶口田制屯田莊田

translations.literal: ○ Household Registers, Land System, Military Colonies, and Estate Lands
translations.idiomatic: ○ Household Registers, Land System, Military Colonies, and Estate Lands

sentences.zh: 太祖籍天下戶口，置戶帖、戶籍，具書名、歲、居地。

translations.literal: The founding emperor registered households throughout the realm, establishing household placards and household registers fully recording names, ages, and places of residence.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor registered households throughout the realm, issuing household placards and compiling household registers that recorded each person's name, age, and place of residence.

sentences.zh: 籍上戶部，帖給之民。

translations.literal: The registers were submitted to the Ministry of Revenue, and the placards were issued to the people.
translations.idiomatic: The registers were filed with the Ministry of Revenue, and the placards were issued to the people.

sentences.zh: 有司歲計其登耗以聞。

translations.literal: Local officials annually calculated increases and decreases and reported them.
translations.idiomatic: Each year local officials calculated gains and losses in the registers and reported them upward.

sentences.zh: 及郊祀，中書省以戶籍陳壇下，薦之天，祭畢而藏之。

translations.literal: At the suburban sacrifices, the Secretariat of State Affairs presented the household registers below the altar, offered them to Heaven, and after the rites were concluded, stored them away.
translations.idiomatic: At the suburban sacrifices, the Secretariat presented the household registers before the altar, offered them to Heaven, and stored them away once the rites were complete.

sentences.zh: 洪武十四年詔天下編賦役黃冊，以一百十戶為一里，推丁糧多者十戶為長，餘百戶為十甲，甲凡十人。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Hongwu, an edict ordered the realm to compile yellow registers of tax and corvée obligations, taking one hundred and ten households as one li, selecting the ten households with the most adult males and grain tax as leaders, and dividing the remaining hundred households into ten jia of ten persons each.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 14, an edict ordered the compilation of yellow registers of tax and corvée obligations throughout the realm. One hundred and ten households formed a li; the ten households with the greatest adult-male and grain-tax obligations became li leaders, and the remaining hundred households were divided into ten jia of ten persons each.

sentences.zh: 歲役裏長一人，甲首一人，董一里一甲之事。

translations.literal: Each year one li chief and one jia head were corvée-appointed to oversee the affairs of one li and one jia respectively.
translations.idiomatic: Each year one li chief and one jia head were appointed by rotation to manage the affairs of their li and jia respectively.

sentences.zh: 先後以丁糧多寡為序，凡十年一週，曰排年。

translations.literal: Order was determined by the amount of adult males and grain tax, completing a full cycle every ten years — this was called the "rotating-year" roster.
translations.idiomatic: Order of service was determined by the amount of adult males and grain tax owed, with a full cycle completed every ten years — this was called the rotating-year roster.

sentences.zh: 在城曰坊，近城曰廂，鄉都曰裏。

translations.literal: In cities they were called fang [wards]; near cities, xiang [suburban districts]; in townships and districts, li.
translations.idiomatic: In cities the units were called wards; near cities, suburban districts; in townships and rural districts, li.

sentences.zh: 裏編為冊，冊首總為一圖。

translations.literal: Each li was compiled into a register, and the summary at the head of the register formed one diagram.
translations.idiomatic: Each li was compiled into a register, with a summary diagram at the head of the volume.

sentences.zh: 鰥寡孤獨不任役者，附十甲後為畸零。

translations.literal: Widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary who could not bear corvée were attached after the ten jia as "odd remainders."
translations.idiomatic: Widowers, widows, orphans, and others living alone who could not bear corvée obligations were listed after the ten jia as odd remainders.

sentences.zh: 僧道給度牒，有田者編冊如民科，無田者亦為畸零。

translations.literal: Monks and Daoists were issued ordination certificates; those with land were registered like commoners and taxed accordingly; those without land were also classified as odd remainders.
translations.idiomatic: Monks and Daoist priests received ordination certificates; those who owned land were registered and taxed like commoners, while those without land were also classified as odd remainders.

sentences.zh: 每十年有司更定其冊，以丁糧增減而升降之。

translations.literal: Every ten years local officials revised the registers, promoting or demoting households according to increases or decreases in adult males and grain tax.
translations.idiomatic: Every ten years local officials revised the registers, adjusting households up or down according to changes in adult males and grain-tax obligations.

sentences.zh: 冊凡四：一上戶部，其三則布政司、府、縣各存一焉。

translations.literal: The registers totaled four copies: one submitted to the Ministry of Revenue, and the other three retained respectively by the provincial administration commission, prefecture, and county.
translations.idiomatic: There were four copies of each register: one submitted to the Ministry of Revenue, and one each retained by the provincial administration commission, the prefecture, and the county.

sentences.zh: 上戶部者，冊面黃紙，故謂之黃冊。

translations.literal: The copy submitted to the Ministry of Revenue had yellow paper covers, hence it was called the yellow register.
translations.idiomatic: The copy sent to the Ministry of Revenue had yellow covers, hence the name yellow register.

sentences.zh: 年終進呈，送後湖東西二庫庋藏之。

translations.literal: At year's end it was submitted to the throne and sent to the eastern and western vaults on Rear Lake for storage.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end it was submitted to the throne and stored in the eastern and western archives on Rear Lake.

sentences.zh: 歲命戶科給事中一人、御史二人、戶部主事四人釐校訛舛。

translations.literal: Each year one supervising secretary from the Revenue Section, two censors, and four principal secretaries from the Ministry of Revenue were appointed to examine and correct errors.
translations.idiomatic: Each year one supervising secretary from the Revenue Section, two censors, and four principal secretaries from the Ministry of Revenue were assigned to examine the registers and correct errors.

sentences.zh: 其後黃冊只具文，有司徵稅、編徭，則自為一冊，曰白冊云。

translations.literal: Later the yellow register became merely a formal document; when local officials collected taxes and compiled corvée obligations, they made their own separate register, called the white register.
translations.idiomatic: Later the yellow register became a mere formality; when local officials collected taxes and compiled corvée obligations, they kept a separate working register called the white register.

sentences.zh: 凡戶三等：曰民，曰軍，曰匠。

translations.literal: Households fell into three categories: commoner, military, and artisan.
translations.idiomatic: Households were divided into three categories: commoner, military, and artisan.

sentences.zh: 民有儒，有醫，有陰陽。

translations.literal: Among commoners were scholars, physicians, and yin-yang diviners.
translations.idiomatic: Among commoners were scholars, physicians, and yin-yang diviners.

sentences.zh: 軍有校尉，有力士，弓、鋪兵。

translations.literal: Among military households were guard officers, strongmen, archers, and sentry troops.
translations.idiomatic: Among military households were guard officers, strongmen, archers, and sentry troops.

sentences.zh: 匠有廚役、裁縫、馬船之類。

translations.literal: Among artisans were kitchen servants, tailors, horse-and-boat workers, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Among artisans were kitchen servants, tailors, horse-and-boat workers, and the like.

sentences.zh: 瀕海有鹽竈。

translations.literal: Along the coast were salt-boiling households.
translations.idiomatic: Along the coast were salt-boiling households.

sentences.zh: 寺有僧，觀有道士。

translations.literal: Temples had monks; abbeys had Daoist priests.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist temples had monks; Daoist abbeys had priests.

sentences.zh: 畢以其業著籍。

translations.literal: All were registered according to their occupation.
translations.idiomatic: All were registered according to their occupation.

sentences.zh: 人戶以籍為斷，禁數姓合戶附籍。

translations.literal: Individual household membership was determined by the register; combining several surnames into one household for registration was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Household membership was determined strictly by the register; combining several surnames into one household for registration was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 漏口、脫戶，許自實。

translations.literal: Those who had omitted persons or evaded registration were permitted to report themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had omitted persons from the register or evaded registration were permitted to report themselves voluntarily.

sentences.zh: 裏設老人，選年高為眾所服者，導民善，平鄉里爭訟。

translations.literal: Each li established an elder, selected from among those advanced in years and respected by the community, to guide people toward goodness and settle neighborhood disputes.
translations.idiomatic: Each li appointed an elder, chosen from among those advanced in years and respected by the community, to guide people toward virtue and settle local disputes.

sentences.zh: 其人戶避徭役者曰逃戶。

translations.literal: Household members who evaded corvée and tax obligations were called fugitive households.
translations.idiomatic: Household members who evaded corvée and tax obligations were called fugitive households.

sentences.zh: 年饑或避兵他徙者曰流民。

translations.literal: Those who migrated elsewhere due to famine or to escape warfare were called floating populations.
translations.idiomatic: Those who migrated elsewhere due to famine or to escape warfare were called floating populations.

sentences.zh: 有故而出僑於外者曰附籍。

translations.literal: Those who left their native place for some reason and sojourned abroad were called attached registrations.
translations.idiomatic: Those who left their native place for some reason and sojourned elsewhere were called attached registrations.

sentences.zh: 朝廷所移民曰移徙。

translations.literal: Populations relocated by the court were called resettlement transfers.
translations.idiomatic: Populations relocated by order of the court were called resettlement transfers.

sentences.zh: 凡逃戶，明初督令還本籍復業，賜復一年。

translations.literal: As for fugitive households, in the early Ming they were compelled to return to their native registers and resume their occupations, and were granted a one-year remission of taxes.
translations.idiomatic: As for fugitive households, in the early Ming they were compelled to return to their native registers and resume their occupations, and were granted a one-year tax remission.

sentences.zh: 老弱不能歸及不願歸者，令在所著籍，授田輸賦。

translations.literal: The aged and infirm who could not return, and those unwilling to return, were ordered to register where they were, granted land, and required to pay taxes.
translations.idiomatic: The aged and infirm who could not return, and those unwilling to return, were registered where they were, granted land, and required to pay taxes.

sentences.zh: 正統時，造逃戶周知冊，核其丁糧。

translations.literal: During the Zhengtong reign, a comprehensive register of fugitive households was compiled to verify their adult males and grain tax.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengtong reign, a comprehensive register of fugitive households was compiled to verify their adult males and grain-tax obligations.

sentences.zh: 凡流民，英宗令勘籍，編甲互保，屬在所裏長管轄之。

translations.literal: As for floating populations, Emperor Yingzong ordered verification of registers, organization into mutual-guarantee jia, and oversight by the local li chief.
translations.idiomatic: As for floating populations, Emperor Yingzong ordered verification of registers, organization into mutual-guarantee jia, and oversight by the local li chief.

sentences.zh: 設撫民佐貳官。

translations.literal: Assistant officials for pacifying the people were established.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant officials for pacifying the people were appointed.

sentences.zh: 歸本者，勞徠安輯，給牛、種、口糧。

translations.literal: Those returning to their native places were welcomed and settled with offers of cattle, seed, and grain rations.
translations.idiomatic: Those returning to their native places were welcomed and settled with offers of cattle, seed, and grain rations.

sentences.zh: 又從河南、山西巡撫于謙言，免流民復業者稅。

translations.literal: Following the recommendation of the Henan and Shanxi Grand Coordinator Yu Qian, taxes were remitted for floating populations who resumed their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Following the recommendation of Yu Qian, Grand Coordinator of Henan and Shanxi, taxes were remitted for floating populations who resumed their occupations.

sentences.zh: 成化初，荊、襄寇亂，流民百萬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chenghua reign, bandits ravaged Jingzhou and Xiangyang, and the floating population reached a million.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chenghua reign, bandits ravaged Jingzhou and Xiangyang, and the floating population reached a million.

sentences.zh: 項忠、楊璿為湖廣巡撫，下令逐之，弗率者戍邊，死者無算。

translations.literal: Xiang Zhong and Yang Xuan, as Grand Coordinators of Huguang, ordered them expelled; those who did not comply were sent to garrison the frontier, and the dead were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Zhong and Yang Xuan, as Grand Coordinators of Huguang, ordered them expelled; those who did not comply were sent to garrison the frontier, and the dead were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 祭酒周洪謨著《流民說》，引東晉時僑置郡縣之法，使近者附籍，遠者設州縣以撫之。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary of the National Academy Zhou Hongmo wrote "On Floating Populations," citing the Eastern Jin practice of establishing provisional commanderies and counties, so that those nearby would attach to local registers while those far away would have prefectures and counties set up to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Hongmo, Grand Secretary of the National Academy, wrote "On Floating Populations," citing the Eastern Jin practice of establishing provisional commanderies and counties so that those nearby could attach to local registers while those farther away would have prefectures and counties set up to settle them.

sentences.zh: 都御史李賓上其說。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Li Bin submitted this proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Li Bin submitted this proposal to the throne.

sentences.zh: 憲宗命原傑出撫，招流民十二萬戶，給閒田，置鄖陽府，立上津等縣統治之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong dispatched Yuan Jie to pacify the region; he recruited 120,000 floating households, granted idle land, established Yunyang Prefecture, and created Shangjin and other counties to govern them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong dispatched Yuan Jie to pacify the region; he recruited 120,000 floating households, granted idle land, established Yunyang Prefecture, and created Shangjin and other counties to govern them.

sentences.zh: 河南巡撫張瑄亦請輯西北流民。

translations.literal: Henan Grand Coordinator Zhang Xuan also requested to settle the floating populations of the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuan, Grand Coordinator of Henan, also requested authority to settle the floating populations of the northwest.

sentences.zh: 帝從其請。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 凡附籍者，正統時，老疾致仕事故官家屬，離本籍千里者許收附，不及千里者發還。

translations.literal: As for attached registrations, during Zhengtong, family members of officials who retired due to age or illness or who left office for cause — if they were more than a thousand li from their native register, they were permitted to attach locally; if less than a thousand li, they were sent back.
translations.idiomatic: As for attached registrations, during Zhengtong family members of officials who retired due to age or illness or who left office for cause were permitted to attach locally if they were more than a thousand li from their native register; if less than a thousand li, they were sent back.

sentences.zh: 景泰中，令民籍者收附，軍、匠、竈役冒民籍者發還。

translations.literal: During the Jingtai reign, civilian registrations were permitted to attach locally; those from military, artisan, or salt-boiler households who falsely claimed civilian registration were sent back.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingtai reign, those with civilian registration were permitted to attach locally; those from military, artisan, or salt-boiler households who falsely claimed civilian status were sent back.

sentences.zh: 其移徙者，明初，當徙蘇、鬆、嘉、湖、杭民之無田者四千餘戶，往耕臨濠，給牛、種、車、糧，以資遣之，三年不徵其稅。

translations.literal: As for resettlement transfers, in the early Ming some four thousand-odd households of landless people from Suzhou, Songjiang, Jiaxing, Huzhou, and Hangzhou were relocated to farm at Linhao; cattle, seed, carts, and grain were provided to assist their move, and taxes were not levied for three years.
translations.idiomatic: As for resettlement transfers, in the early Ming more than four thousand landless households from Suzhou, Songjiang, Jiaxing, Huzhou, and Hangzhou were relocated to farm at Linhao; cattle, seed, carts, and grain were provided to support the move, and taxes were not levied for three years.

sentences.zh: 徐達平沙漠，徙北平山後民三萬五千八百餘戶，散處諸府衛，籍為軍者給衣糧，民給田。

translations.literal: When Xu Da pacified the desert, 35,800-odd households from beyond the mountains of northern Ping [Beijing area] were relocated and dispersed among various prefectures and guard posts; those registered as military were given clothing and grain, commoners were given land.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Da pacified the desert, more than 35,800 households from beyond the mountains of northern Ping were relocated and dispersed among various prefectures and guard posts; those registered as military received clothing and grain, while commoners received land.

sentences.zh: 又以沙漠遺民三萬二千八百餘戶屯田北平，置屯二百五十四，開地千三百四十三頃。

translations.literal: Another 32,800-odd desert remnant households were settled in military colonies in northern Ping, establishing 254 colonies and opening 1,343 qing of land.
translations.idiomatic: Another 32,800-odd desert remnant households were settled in military colonies in northern Ping, establishing 254 colonies and opening 1,343 qing of land.

sentences.zh: 復徙江南民十四萬於鳳陽。

translations.literal: Jiangnan people numbering 140,000 were again relocated to Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Another 140,000 people from Jiangnan were relocated to Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 戶部郎中劉九皋言：「古狹鄉之民，聽遷之寬鄉，欲地無遺利，人無失業也。

translations.literal: Revenue Section Director Liu Jiugao said: "In antiquity, people from narrow districts were permitted to move to spacious ones, intending that no land go unused and no person lose employment."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jiugao, a director in the Ministry of Revenue, said: "In antiquity, people from crowded districts were permitted to move to less populated ones, so that no land would lie unused and no one would be without livelihood."

sentences.zh: 」太祖採其議，遷山凱撒、潞民於河北。

translations.literal: " The founding emperor adopted this proposal and relocated the peoples of Shankaisha and Lu to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: " The founding emperor adopted this proposal and relocated the peoples of Shankaisha and Lu to Hebei.

sentences.zh: 眾屢徙浙西及山西民於滁、和、北平、山東、河南。

translations.literal: Populations were repeatedly moved from western Zhejiang and Shanxi to Chuzhou, Hezhou, northern Ping, Shandong, and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Populations were repeatedly moved from western Zhejiang and Shanxi to Chuzhou, Hezhou, northern Ping, Shandong, and Henan.

sentences.zh: 又徙登、萊、青民於東昌、兗州。

translations.literal: People from Dengzhou, Laizhou, and Qingzhou were also relocated to Dongchang and Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: People from Dengzhou, Laizhou, and Qingzhou were also relocated to Dongchang and Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 又徙直隸、浙江民二萬戶於京師，充倉腳夫。

translations.literal: Another 20,000 households from Zhili and Zhejiang were relocated to the capital to serve as granary porters.
translations.idiomatic: Another 20,000 households from Zhili and Zhejiang were relocated to the capital to serve as granary porters.

sentences.zh: 太祖時徙民最多，其間有以罪徙者。

translations.literal: Relocations were most numerous during the founding emperor's reign; among them were some moved as punishment for crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Relocations were most numerous under the founding emperor; among them were some moved as punishment for crimes.

sentences.zh: 建文帝命武康伯徐理往北平度地處之。

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen ordered Baron Wukang Xu Li to go to northern Ping to survey land and settle them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen ordered Xu Li, Baron of Wukang, to go to northern Ping to survey land and settle the relocated population.

sentences.zh: 成祖核太原、平陽、澤、潞、遼、沁、汾丁多田少及無田之家，分其丁口以實北平。

translations.literal: Emperor Chengzu examined households in Taiyuan, Pingyang, Ze, Lu, Liao, Qin, and Fen with many adult males but little land or no land at all, and divided their population to populate northern Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Chengzu examined households in Taiyuan, Pingyang, Ze, Lu, Liao, Qin, and Fen that had many adult males but little land or none at all, and divided their population to populate northern Ping.

sentences.zh: 自是以後，移徙者鮮矣。

translations.literal: From this time onward, resettlement transfers became rare.
translations.idiomatic: From this time onward, resettlement transfers became rare.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖設養濟院收無告者，月給糧。

translations.literal: Initially, the founding emperor established relief hospices to take in those with no one to care for them, providing monthly grain rations.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, the founding emperor established relief hospices to take in those with no one to care for them, providing monthly grain rations.

sentences.zh: 設漏澤園葬貧民。

translations.literal: Public burial grounds [Louze Gardens] were established to bury the poor.
translations.idiomatic: Public burial grounds were established to bury the poor.

sentences.zh: 天下府州縣立義塚。

translations.literal: Benevolent burial plots were established in prefectures, departments, and counties throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolent burial plots were established in prefectures, departments, and counties throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 又行養老之政，民年八十以上賜爵。

translations.literal: Policies for supporting the aged were also implemented; commoners aged eighty and above were granted honorary ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Policies for supporting the aged were also implemented; commoners aged eighty and above were granted honorary ranks.

sentences.zh: 復下詔優恤遭難兵民。

translations.literal: Edicts were again issued granting generous relief to soldiers and civilians who had suffered hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts were again issued granting generous relief to soldiers and civilians who had suffered hardship.

sentences.zh: 然懲元末豪強侮貧弱，立法多右貧抑富。

translations.literal: Yet, as punishment for the powerful local magnates of the late Yuan who oppressed the poor and weak, legislation largely favored the poor and checked the rich.
translations.idiomatic: Yet, reacting against the powerful local magnates of the late Yuan who had oppressed the poor and weak, legislation largely favored the poor and restrained the rich.

sentences.zh: 嘗命戶部籍浙江等九布政司、應天十八府州富民萬四千三百餘戶，以次召見，徙其家以實京師，謂之富戶。

translations.literal: He once ordered the Ministry of Revenue to register 14,300-odd wealthy households from the nine provincial commissions including Zhejiang and the eighteen prefectures and departments of Yingtian, summoning them in succession and relocating their families to populate the capital — these were called wealthy households.
translations.idiomatic: He once ordered the Ministry of Revenue to register more than 14,300 wealthy households from the nine provincial commissions including Zhejiang and the eighteen prefectures and departments of Yingtian, summoning them in succession and relocating their families to populate the capital — these were called wealthy households.

sentences.zh: 成祖時，復選應天、浙江富民三千戶，充北京宛、大二縣廂長，附籍京師，仍應本籍徭役。

translations.literal: During Chengzu's reign, 3,000 wealthy households from Yingtian and Zhejiang were again selected to serve as suburban district chiefs of Wanping and Daxing counties in Beijing; they attached their registration to the capital but still fulfilled corvée obligations in their native registers.
translations.idiomatic: During Chengzu's reign, 3,000 wealthy households from Yingtian and Zhejiang were again selected to serve as suburban district chiefs of Wanping and Daxing counties in Beijing; they attached their registration to the capital but still fulfilled corvée obligations in their native registers.

sentences.zh: 供給日久，貧乏逃竄，輒選其本籍殷實戶僉補。

translations.literal: As support duties dragged on, impoverishment and flight ensued, and wealthy households from their native registers were conscripted to fill vacancies.
translations.idiomatic: As support duties dragged on, many grew impoverished and fled, and wealthy households from their native registers were conscripted to fill the vacancies.

sentences.zh: 宣德間定制，逃者發邊充軍，官司鄰裏隱匿者俱坐罪。

translations.literal: During the Xuande reign regulations were fixed: fugitives were sent to the frontier as soldiers, and officials, neighbors, and li associates who concealed them were all punished.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuande reign regulations were fixed: fugitives were sent to the frontier as soldiers, and officials, neighbors, and li associates who concealed them were all punished.

sentences.zh: 弘治五年始免解在逃富戶，每戶徵銀三兩，與廂民助役。

translations.literal: Beginning in the fifth year of Hongzhi, wealthy households in flight were no longer compelled to report; each household paid three taels of silver to assist corvée duties for suburban residents.
translations.idiomatic: Beginning in Hongzhi 5, wealthy households in flight were no longer compelled to report in person; each household paid three taels of silver to assist corvée duties for suburban residents.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中減為二兩，以充邊餉。

translations.literal: During the Jiajing reign this was reduced to two taels, allocated to frontier provisions.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiajing reign this was reduced to two taels, allocated to frontier provisions.

sentences.zh: 太祖立法之意，本仿漢徙富民實關中之制，其後事久弊生，遂為厲階。

translations.literal: The founding emperor's intent in legislating was originally to emulate the Han practice of relocating wealthy households to populate the Guanzhong region; later, as time passed abuses arose, and it became a source of harm.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor's intent in legislating was originally to emulate the Han practice of relocating wealthy households to populate the Guanzhong region; over time abuses arose, and the policy became a source of harm.

sentences.zh: 戶口之數，增減不一，其可考者，洪武二十六年，天下戶一千六十五萬二千八百七十，口六千五十四萬五千八百十二。

translations.literal: The numbers of households varied in increase and decrease; among those that can be verified, in the twenty-sixth year of Hongwu there were 10,652,870 households throughout the realm and 60,545,812 persons.
translations.idiomatic: Household numbers rose and fell unevenly; among figures that can be verified, in Hongwu 26 there were 10,652,870 households throughout the realm and 60,545,812 persons.

sentences.zh: 弘治四年，戶九百十一萬三千四百四十六，口五千三百二十八萬一千一百五十八。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongzhi: 9,113,446 households and 53,281,158 persons.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 4: 9,113,446 households and 53,281,158 persons.

sentences.zh: 萬曆六年，戶一千六十二萬一千四百三十六，口六千六十九萬二千八百五十六。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wanli: 10,621,436 households and 60,692,856 persons.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 6: 10,621,436 households and 60,692,856 persons.

sentences.zh: 太祖當兵燹之後，戶口顧極盛。

translations.literal: Remarkably, under the founding emperor, after the devastation of warfare, household registers were at their peak.
translations.idiomatic: Remarkably, under the founding emperor, household registers reached their peak even after the devastation of warfare.

sentences.zh: 其後承平日久，反不及焉。

translations.literal: In the long peace that followed, they actually fell short of this.
translations.idiomatic: In the long peace that followed, they actually fell short of this.

sentences.zh: 靖難兵起，淮以北鞠為茂草，其時民數反增於前。

translations.literal: When the Jingnan rebellion broke out, the region north of the Huai River was trampled into wild grass, yet at that time the population count actually increased over the previous figure.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingnan rebellion broke out, the region north of the Huai River was trampled into wild grass, yet the population count at that time actually rose above the previous figure.

sentences.zh: 後乃遞減，至天順間為最衰。

translations.literal: Afterward it declined in succession, reaching its lowest point during the Tianshun reign.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward it declined in succession, reaching its lowest point during the Tianshun reign.

sentences.zh: 成、弘繼盛，正德以後又減。

translations.literal: Chenghua and Hongzhi saw renewed prosperity; after Zhengde there was decline again.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua and Hongzhi saw renewed prosperity; after Zhengde there was decline again.

sentences.zh: 戶口所以減者，周忱謂：「投倚於豪門，或冒匠竄兩京，或冒引賈四方，舉家舟居，莫可蹤跡也。

translations.literal: Zhou Chen explained why household registers declined: "Some attach themselves to powerful clans; some falsely claim artisan status and slip into the two capitals; some falsely pose as merchants and travel the four directions — whole families live aboard boats with no trace to be found."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chen explained why household registers declined: "Some attach themselves to powerful clans; some falsely claim artisan status and slip into the two capitals; some falsely pose as merchants and travel in every direction — whole families live aboard boats with no trace to be found."

sentences.zh: 」而要之，戶口增減，由於政令張弛。

translations.literal: " In essence, the rise and fall of registered households depended on whether government orders were enforced strictly or laxly.
translations.idiomatic: " In essence, the rise and fall of registered households depended on whether government orders were enforced strictly or laxly.

sentences.zh: 故宣宗嘗與羣臣論歷代戶口，以為「其盛也，本於休養生息，其衰也，由土木兵戎」，殆篤論云。

translations.literal: Therefore the Xuande Emperor once discussed with his officials the household registers of successive dynasties, holding that "their flourishing had its root in nourishing the people and allowing them to recover; their decline came from construction projects and warfare." This was indeed a penetrating judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Xuande Emperor once debated with his ministers the rise and fall of population across the ages. His verdict was that prosperity rested on letting the people rest and recover, while decline came from grand construction and incessant war — a remark that cuts to the heart of the matter.

sentences.zh: 明土田之制，凡二等：曰官田，曰民田。

translations.literal: The Ming system for land and fields had two categories in all: called official land and private land.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming, all land fell into two categories: official land and private land.

sentences.zh: 初，官田皆宋、元時入官田地。

translations.literal: At first, official land was all land that had entered government ownership during the Song and Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, official land consisted entirely of fields that had been taken into government hands under the Song and Yuan.

sentences.zh: 厥後有還官田，沒官田，斷入官田，學田，皇莊，牧馬草場，城鵒需苜蓿地，牲地，園陵墳地，公佔隙地，諸王、公主、勳戚、大臣、內監、寺觀賜乞莊田，百官職田，邊臣養廉田，軍、民、商屯田，通謂之官田。

translations.literal: Thereafter there were restored-to-official land, confiscated official land, adjudicated-and-entered official land, school land, imperial estates, horse-pasture fields, lands for city pigeons requiring alfalfa, sacrificial lands, garden tomb and grave lands, publicly occupied vacant lands, estate lands granted or begged by princes, princesses, meritorious relatives, great ministers, eunuchs, and temples, official salary lands for all officials, integrity-supporting lands for frontier officials, military, civilian, and merchant colony lands — all collectively called official land.
translations.idiomatic: Later the category expanded to include land restored to the state, confiscated land, land adjudicated into government hands, school fields, imperial estates, cavalry pastures, pigeon-loft hayfields, sacrificial grounds, mausoleum plots, vacant plots seized for public use, estates granted to or solicited by princes, princesses, imperial in-laws, high ministers, eunuchs, and monasteries, salary allotments for officials, "integrity stipend" fields for frontier administrators, and military, civilian, and merchant colony farms — all of these were collectively termed official land.

sentences.zh: 其餘為民田。

translations.literal: The remainder was private land.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else counted as private land.

sentences.zh: 元季喪亂，版籍多亡，田賦無準。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan, chaos and disorder prevailed; registers were largely lost, and land taxes had no standard.
translations.idiomatic: In the final years of the Yuan, war and turmoil destroyed most land records, leaving field taxes without any reliable basis.

sentences.zh: 明太祖即帝位，遣周鑄等百六十四人，核浙西田畝，定其賦稅。

translations.literal: When the Ming Founder ascended the throne, he dispatched Zhou Zhuo and one hundred sixty-four others to verify the field acreage of western Zhejiang and fix its taxes and levies.
translations.idiomatic: Upon taking the throne, the Hongwu Emperor sent Zhou Zhuo and 164 others to survey field acreage in western Zhejiang and set tax rates accordingly.

sentences.zh: 復命戶部核實天下土田。

translations.literal: He further ordered the Ministry of Revenue to verify all land throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the Ministry of Revenue to verify landholding throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 而兩浙富民畏避徭役，大率以田產寄他戶，謂之鐵腳詭寄。

translations.literal: But wealthy households in the two Zhejiangs, fearing and evading corvée labor, for the most part registered their lands under other households — this was called "iron-foot fraudulent registration."
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy households in the Jiangnan region, seeking to dodge corvée duties, commonly registered their property under someone else's name — a practice known as "iron-foot ghost registration."

sentences.zh: 洪武二十年命國子生武淳等分行州縣，隨糧定區。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Hongwu, [the emperor] ordered Imperial Academy students such as Wu Chun to go out to the various prefectures and counties, delimiting districts according to grain quotas.
translations.idiomatic: In 1387, he dispatched Imperial Academy students including Wu Chun to the counties and prefectures to draw tax districts based on grain quotas.

sentences.zh: 區設糧長四人，量度田畝方圓，次以字型大小，悉書主名及田之丈尺，編類為冊，狀如魚鱗，號曰魚鱗圖冊。

translations.literal: In each district four grain wardens were established; they measured the length and breadth of fields, arranged them by the size of character shapes, fully recorded owners' names and the dimensions of each field, compiled them into a register shaped like fish scales, called the fish-scale land register.
translations.idiomatic: Each district appointed four grain wardens who measured every plot, arranged parcels on the map in descending size, recorded the owner's name and exact dimensions, and compiled the result into a register whose overlapping plots resembled fish scales — the famous yulin tuce, or fish-scale land register.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔天下編黃冊，以戶為主，詳具舊管、新收、開除、實在之數為四柱式。

translations.literal: Earlier, an edict had ordered the realm to compile yellow registers, organized by household, with a detailed four-column format recording numbers previously held, newly added, removed, and actually present.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the throne had ordered household registers compiled empire-wide — the huangce, or yellow books — organized by household with four columns tracking prior holdings, new acquisitions, deductions, and present totals.

sentences.zh: 而魚鱗圖冊以土田為主，諸原阪、墳衍、下隰、沃瘠、沙鹵之別畢具。

translations.literal: The fish-scale register, by contrast, was organized by land and fields, with all distinctions among uplands, slopes, low wetlands, fertility, barrenness, sandy and saline soils fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The fish-scale register, by contrast, was organized by land rather than by household, cataloguing every distinction between upland and slope, marsh and plain, rich soil and poor, sandy and saline ground.

sentences.zh: 魚鱗冊為經，土田之訟質焉。

translations.literal: The fish-scale register served as the warp; land disputes were adjudicated by it.
translations.idiomatic: The fish-scale register served as the authoritative record against which land disputes were judged.

sentences.zh: 黃冊為緯，賦役之法定焉。

translations.literal: The yellow register served as the weft; tax and corvée regulations were fixed by it.
translations.idiomatic: The yellow register fixed the basis for taxes and labor obligations.

sentences.zh: 凡質賣田土，備書稅糧科則，官為籍記之，毋令產去稅存以為民害。

translations.literal: Whenever land was sold or pledged, the tax grain schedule was fully recorded and registered by the government, lest the property pass to a new owner while the tax obligation remained on the old one, harming the people.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever land changed hands, the tax schedule had to be fully recorded and entered in the official registers — a safeguard against the common abuse where property transferred but tax liability stayed behind, to the seller's ruin.

sentences.zh: 又以中原田多蕪，命省臣議，計民授田。

translations.literal: Further, because fields in the Central Plains were largely fallow, he ordered provincial ministers to deliberate on allocating land to the people according to a calculated scheme.
translations.idiomatic: Because much farmland in the Central Plains lay abandoned, he ordered provincial officials to devise a scheme for allocating land to settlers.

sentences.zh: 設司農司，開治河南，掌其事。

translations.literal: A Directorate of Agriculture was established, with its work centered on Henan, to manage the matter.
translations.idiomatic: A Directorate of Agriculture was set up with its headquarters in Henan to administer the program.

sentences.zh: 臨濠之田，驗其丁力，計畝給之，毋許兼併。

translations.literal: For the fields at Linhuai, [land was] allotted by measured acreage according to available adult labor, and consolidation was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: At Linhuai, land was apportioned by measuring each household's labor capacity, acre by acre — consolidation was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 北方近城地多不治，召民耕，人給十五畝，蔬地二畝，免租三年。

translations.literal: In the north, much land near cities lay uncultivated; the people were summoned to farm it, with fifteen mu per person and two mu of vegetable plots, rent-free for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Much of the land near northern cities lay idle; settlers were recruited to cultivate it, with fifteen mu of grain land plus two mu for vegetables apiece, rent-free for three years.

sentences.zh: 每歲中書省奏天下墾田數，少者畝以千計，多者至二十餘萬。

translations.literal: Each year the Central Secretariat reported nationwide figures for reclaimed land — in small cases counted in thousands of mu, in large cases reaching more than two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the Central Secretariat reported reclaimed acreage empire-wide — sometimes a few thousand mu, sometimes more than 200,000.

sentences.zh: 官給牛及農具者，乃收其稅，額外墾荒者永不起科。

translations.literal: Where the government supplied oxen and farm tools, taxes were collected; land reclaimed beyond the quota was forever exempt from assessment.
translations.idiomatic: Settlers who received oxen and tools from the state paid tax on their allotment, but any land they cleared beyond that quota was permanently tax-exempt.

sentences.zh: 二十六年核天下土田，總八百五十萬七千六百二十三頃，蓋駸駸無棄土矣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, land throughout the realm was tallied, totaling 8,507,623 qing — by then nearly no land lay abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: A national land survey in 1393 counted 8,507,623 qing — by then, scarcely an acre of cultivable soil remained idle.

sentences.zh: 凡田以近郭為上地，迤遠為中地、下地。

translations.literal: In general, fields near the city walls were classified as upper-grade land; progressively farther away as middle-grade and lower-grade.
translations.idiomatic: Fields nearest the city walls ranked as top-grade; farther out as middling, and still farther as inferior.

sentences.zh: 五尺為步，步二百四十為畝，畝百為頃。

translations.literal: Five chi made one bu; 240 bu made one mu; 100 mu made one qing.
translations.idiomatic: The standard was five chi to the pace, 240 paces to the mu, and 100 mu to the qing.

sentences.zh: 太祖仍元裏社制，河北諸州縣土著者以社分裏甲，遷民分屯之地以屯分裏甲。

translations.literal: The Founder retained the Yuan system of li and she: in the prefectures and counties of Hebei, native inhabitants were organized into li and jia by she; in areas where resettled people were divided into colonies, li and jia were organized by colony units.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu preserved the Yuan li-and-she system: in Hebei, native residents were grouped into li and jia by community (she); resettled colonists were grouped by colony unit (tun).

sentences.zh: 社民先佔畝廣，屯民新佔畝狹，故屯地謂之小畝，社地謂之廣畝。

translations.literal: Community residents had claimed their acreage early and received broad mu; colonists newly claiming land received narrow mu — hence colony land was called "small mu" and community land "broad mu."
translations.idiomatic: Natives who had claimed land early held plots measured by generous mu; newer colonists got cramped plots — so colony land was called "small mu" and native community land "broad mu."

sentences.zh: 至宣德間，墾荒田永不起科及洿下斥鹵無糧者，皆核入賦額，數溢於舊。

translations.literal: By the Xuande reign, permanently tax-exempt reclaimed wasteland and low saline lands yielding no grain were all incorporated into the tax quota; the figures exceeded the old totals.
translations.idiomatic: By the Xuande era, previously tax-exempt reclaimed land and low-lying saline plots that yielded nothing had all been folded into the tax rolls, swelling totals beyond earlier figures.

sentences.zh: 有司乃以大畝當小畝以符舊額，有數畝當一畝者。

translations.literal: Local officials then used large mu in place of small mu to match the old quota — in some cases several mu counted as one.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials compensated by counting several "small mu" as one "large mu" to match old quotas — sometimes several actual mu equaled one official mu.

sentences.zh: 步尺參差不一，人得以意贏縮，土地不均，未有如北方者。

translations.literal: Paces and rulers varied irregularly, allowing people to expand or contract at will; nowhere was land distribution so unequal as in the north.
translations.idiomatic: Measuring rods differed from place to place, leaving room for manipulation; nowhere was land distribution more skewed than in the north.

sentences.zh: 貴州田無頃畝尺籍，悉徵之土官。

translations.literal: In Guizhou there were no registers of qing, mu, and measures; taxes were entirely levied through native chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou had no standardized land registers at all; taxes were collected entirely through local native chiefs.

sentences.zh: 而諸處土田，日久頗淆亂，與黃冊不符。

translations.literal: Yet over time land registers everywhere grew quite confused and no longer matched the yellow registers.
translations.idiomatic: Over time, land records across the empire fell into disarray and no longer matched the yellow registers.

sentences.zh: 弘治十五年，天下土田止四百二十二萬八千五十八頃，官田視民田得七之一。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Hongzhi, land throughout the realm amounted to only 4,228,058 qing; official land compared to private land was about one in seven.
translations.idiomatic: By 1502, registered land had fallen to just 4,228,058 qing — official land comprising roughly one-seventh of private land.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年，霍韞奉命修會典，言：「自洪武迄弘治百四十年，天下額田已減強半，而湖廣、河南、廣東失額尤多。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jiajing, Huo Yun was ordered to revise the Collected Statutes and stated: "From Hongwu through Hongzhi, one hundred forty years — registered quota land has been reduced by more than half, and losses are especially great in Huguang, Henan, and Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1529, Huo Yun, charged with revising the Collected Statutes, reported: "In the 140 years since Hongwu, registered land quota has been cut by more than half — with the steepest losses in Huguang, Henan, and Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 非撥給於王府，則欺隱於猾民。

translations.literal: If not apportioned to princely establishments, then concealed by cunning commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Lost either to princely fief allocations or to concealment by sharp-dealing landowners.

sentences.zh: 廣東無籓府，非欺隱即委棄於寇賊矣。

translations.literal: Guangdong has no princely fiefs — [the land] was either concealed or abandoned to bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong had no princely estates to absorb the shortfall — whatever was missing had either been hidden or abandoned to bandits.

sentences.zh: 司國計者，可不究心？

translations.literal: Those charged with managing the state's finances — can they fail to investigate this with care?
translations.idiomatic: Surely those responsible for the national accounts could not afford to ignore this?

sentences.zh: 」是時，桂萼、郭弘化、唐能、簡霄先後疏請核實田畝，而顧鼎臣請履畝丈量，丈量之議由此起。

translations.literal: At this time Gui E, Guo Honghua, Tang Neng, and Jian Xiao successively memorialized requesting verification of field acreage, while Gu Dingchen requested on-site mu-by-mu surveying — and the proposal for land measurement arose from this.
translations.idiomatic: Gui E, Guo Honghua, Tang Neng, and Jian Xiao then petitioned in succession for a land audit; Gu Dingchen called for field-by-field surveying — and the nationwide measurement campaign was born.

sentences.zh: 江西安福、河南裕州首行之，而法未詳具，人多疑憚。

translations.literal: Anfu in Jiangxi and Yuzhou in Henan were the first to implement it, but the regulations were not fully detailed and many people were suspicious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Anfu in Jiangxi and Yuzhou in Henan piloted the scheme first, but the procedures were incomplete and met widespread suspicion.

sentences.zh: 其後福建諸州縣，為經、緯二冊，其法頗詳。

translations.literal: Thereafter various prefectures and counties in Fujian compiled warp and weft registers, with methods that were fairly detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Fujian counties developed paired warp-and-weft registers with considerably more detailed procedures.

sentences.zh: 然率以地為主，田多者猶得上下其手。

translations.literal: Yet as these generally took land as the primary unit, those with extensive holdings could still manipulate the outcome.
translations.idiomatic: But because registers were still organized by land rather than by household, wealthy landowners could still manipulate the figures.

sentences.zh: 神宗初，建昌知府許孚遠為歸戶冊，則以田從人，法簡而密矣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shenzong reign, Xu Fuyuan, prefect of Jianchang, created the "return-to-household register," organizing fields according to the person — a method both simple and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wanli's reign, Jianchang prefect Xu Fuyuan introduced the "return-to-household register," tying fields to their owners — simpler and tighter than what came before.

sentences.zh: 萬曆六年，帝用大學士張居正議，天下田畝通行丈量，限三載竣事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wanli, the emperor adopted the proposal of Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng for universal land measurement throughout the realm, with a three-year deadline for completion.
translations.idiomatic: In 1578, the emperor adopted Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng's plan for a nationwide land survey, to be completed within three years.

sentences.zh: 用開方法，以徑圍乘除，畸零截補。

translations.literal: Using the "opening-square method," multiplying and dividing by diameter and perimeter, irregular parcels were trimmed or supplemented.
translations.idiomatic: Surveyors used geometric formulas — multiplying and dividing diameters and perimeters — to calculate irregular plots by trimming corners and filling gaps.

sentences.zh: 於是豪猾不得欺隱，裏甲免賠累，而小民無虛糧。

translations.literal: Thereupon the powerful and cunning could not conceal [land]; li and jia heads were spared covering shortfalls, and common people were free of phantom tax obligations.
translations.idiomatic: The wealthy could no longer hide land; village heads were no longer liable for others' shortfalls; and ordinary peasants were freed from paying tax on land they did not hold.

sentences.zh: 總計田數七百一萬三千九百七十六頃，視弘治時贏三百萬頃。

translations.literal: The total field count was 7,013,976 qing — three million qing more than in the Hongzhi era.
translations.idiomatic: The survey counted 7,013,976 qing — three million more than the Hongzhi figure.

sentences.zh: 然居正尚綜核，頗以溢額為功。

translations.literal: Yet Zhang Juzheng valued strict accounting and regarded surplus quota as an achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng, however, prized tight fiscal control and treated inflated totals as a mark of success.

sentences.zh: 有司爭改小弓以求田多，或掊克見田以充虛額。

translations.literal: Local officials competed to shorten measuring rods to make fields appear larger, or squeezed existing fields to fill phantom quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Officials shortened measuring rods to inflate acreage, or squeezed peasants' existing plots to meet phantom quotas.

sentences.zh: 北直隸、湖廣、大同、宣府，遂先後按溢額田增賦云。

translations.literal: Zhili, Huguang, Datong, and Xuanfu thereupon successively increased taxes according to surplus quota land.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili, Huguang, Datong, and Xuanfu soon raised tax rates on the newly "discovered" surplus land.

sentences.zh: 屯田之制：曰軍屯，曰民屯。

translations.literal: The system of colony land had two kinds: military colonies and civilian colonies.
translations.idiomatic: The colony-farm system had two branches: military colonies and civilian colonies.

sentences.zh: 太祖初，立民兵萬戶府，寓兵於農，其法最善。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Founder, a militia Myriad-Households Office was established, embedding soldiers among farmers — this method was the finest.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongwu's reign, a militia headquarters was established to embed troops among farmers — the finest version of the policy.

sentences.zh: 又令諸將屯兵龍江諸處，惟康茂才績最，乃下令褒之，因以申飭將士。

translations.literal: He also ordered various generals to station troops for colony farming in places such as Longjiang; only Kang Maocai's results were the best, so an order was issued to praise him, thereby admonishing the officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Generals were also ordered to establish farming garrisons along the Longjiang; Kang Maocai's colony outperformed all others and was publicly commended as an example to the rest.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，中書省請稅太原、朔州屯卒，命勿徵。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu, the Central Secretariat requested to tax garrison colonists at Taiyuan and Shuozhou; [the emperor] ordered that no tax be levied.
translations.idiomatic: In 1370, when the Central Secretariat proposed taxing colonists at Taiyuan and Shuozhou, the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 明年，中書省言：「河南、山東、北平、陝西、山西及直隸淮安諸府屯田，凡官給牛種者十稅五，自備者十稅三。

translations.literal: The following year the Central Secretariat stated: "For colony fields in Henan, Shandong, Beiping, Shaanxi, Shanxi, and the Huai'an prefectures of direct administration — where the government supplies oxen and seed, a tax of five parts in ten; where [farmers] supply their own, three parts in ten.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Secretariat proposed: "For colony farms in Henan, Shandong, Beiping, Shaanxi, Shanxi, and Huai'an — those receiving oxen and seed from the state would pay a fifty-percent rate; self-supplying colonists, thirty percent.

sentences.zh: 」詔且勿徵，三年後畝收租一斗。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that no tax be levied for the time being; after three years, one dou per mu would be collected as rent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deferred collection; after three years the rate would be one dou per mu.

sentences.zh: 六年，太僕丞樑埜仙帖木爾言：「寧夏境內及四川西南至船城，東北至塔灘，相去八百里，土膏沃，宜招集流亡屯田。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Vice Director of the Imperial Stud Liangye Xiantiemuer stated: "Within Ningxia and from southwestern Sichuan to Chuancheng, northeast to Tatai — eight hundred li apart — the soil is rich and fertile; it is suitable to summon displaced people for colony farming.
translations.idiomatic: In 1373, Vice Director of the Imperial Stud Liangye Xiantiemuer reported: "From Ningxia across eight hundred li to Chuancheng in southwest Sichuan and Tatai in the northeast, the soil is rich and fit for resettling refugees as colonists.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: [The proposal] was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 是時，遣鄧愈、湯和諸將屯陝西、彰德、汝甯、北平、永平，徙山西真定民屯鳳陽。

translations.literal: At this time, generals such as Deng Yu and Tang He were dispatched to establish colonies in Shaanxi, Zhangde, Runing, Beiping, and Yongping; people from Zhending in Shanxi were resettled to colonize at Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yu, Tang He, and other generals were sent to establish colonies in Shaanxi, Zhangde, Runing, Beiping, and Yongping, while settlers from Zhending in Shanxi were relocated to farm around Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 又因海運餉遼有溺死者，遂益講屯政，天下衛所州縣軍民皆事墾闢矣。

translations.literal: Also because there were drowning deaths in the sea transport of provisions to Liaodong, colony policy was further strengthened, and throughout the realm guard units, prefectures, counties, soldiers, and civilians all turned to opening new land.
translations.idiomatic: After sailors drowned on supply runs to Liaodong, colony policy was intensified until soldiers and civilians across the empire were all engaged in land reclamation.

sentences.zh: 其制，移民就寬鄉，或召募或罪徙者為民屯，皆領之有司，而軍屯則領之衛所。

translations.literal: Under the system, people were relocated to less crowded districts; those recruited or transported as convicts formed civilian colonies, all overseen by civil officials, while military colonies were overseen by guard units.
translations.idiomatic: Settlers moved to less crowded regions; recruits and convict exiles formed civilian colonies under civil administration, while military colonies fell under guard-unit command.

sentences.zh: 邊地，三分守城，七分屯種。

translations.literal: On frontier lands, three parts guarded the cities, seven parts farmed.
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier, thirty percent of troops garrisoned the walls and seventy percent farmed.

sentences.zh: 內地，二分守城，八分屯種。

translations.literal: In the interior, two parts guarded the cities, eight parts farmed.
translations.idiomatic: In the interior, twenty percent garrisoned and eighty percent farmed.

sentences.zh: 每軍受田五十畝為一分，給耕牛、農具，教樹植，復租賦，遣官勸輸，誅侵暴之吏。

translations.literal: Each soldier received fifty mu as one share; plow oxen and farm tools were supplied, tree planting was taught, rents and levies were reduced, officials were dispatched to encourage delivery, and officers guilty of oppression were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Each soldier received a fifty-mu allotment; the state supplied oxen and tools, taught arboriculture, reduced rents, dispatched officials to supervise deliveries, and punished corrupt local officers.

sentences.zh: 初畝稅一斗。

translations.literal: At first, the tax was one dou per mu.
translations.idiomatic: The initial rate was one dou per mu.

sentences.zh: 三十五年定科則：軍田一分，正糧十二石，貯屯倉，聽本軍自支，餘糧為本衛所官軍俸糧。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year the tax schedule was fixed: for one military share, twelve shi of standard grain were stored in the colony granary, for the use of the colony unit itself; surplus grain served as salary grain for the officers and soldiers of the parent guard unit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1402 the quota was fixed: each fifty-mu share owed twelve shi of grain to the colony granary for the unit's own use; surplus went to supplement guard-unit pay.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，定屯田官軍賞罰例：歲食米十二石外餘六石為率，多者賞鈔，缺者罰俸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle, reward and punishment regulations for colony officers and soldiers were established: beyond the twelve shi of rice consumed per year, six shi surplus was the standard — excess earned paper-money rewards, shortfall incurred salary penalties.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongle, performance standards were set: beyond the twelve shi needed for subsistence, six shi surplus was the target — exceeding it earned a cash reward, falling short meant a pay cut.

sentences.zh: 又以田肥瘠不同，法宜有別，命官軍各種樣田，以其歲收之數相考較。

translations.literal: Further, because fields differed in fertility, the law should also differ; officers and soldiers were ordered each to plant sample fields, and their annual yields were compared against one another.
translations.idiomatic: Because soil quality varied, each unit was required to plant sample plots and compare annual yields.

sentences.zh: 太原左衛千戶陳淮所種樣田，每軍餘糧二十三石，帝命重賞之。

translations.literal: The sample fields planted by Chen Huai, chiliarch of Taiyuan Left Guard, yielded twenty-three shi surplus grain per soldier; the emperor ordered him lavishly rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Huai of Taiyuan Left Guard produced twenty-three shi surplus per soldier from his sample plots; the emperor ordered him lavishly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 寧夏總兵何福積谷尤多，賜敕褒美。

translations.literal: Ningxia supreme commander He Fu accumulated grain in especially large amounts and was granted an edict of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Ningxia commander He Fu amassed an exceptional grain surplus and received an imperial commendation.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書鬱新言：「湖廣諸衛收糧不一種，請以米為準。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Yu Xin stated: "The various guards in Huguang collect grain of different kinds; I request that rice be taken as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue Yu Xin noted: "Huguang guard units collect grain in many varieties; I propose standardizing on rice equivalents.

sentences.zh: 凡粟穀穈黍大麥蕎穄二石，稻穀薥秫二石五斗，穇稗三石，皆準米一石。

translations.literal: In all, two shi of millet, panicled millet, broomcorn millet, barley, buckwheat, and kaoliang equal one shi of rice; two shi five dou of husked rice, sorghum, and glutinous millet; three shi of coix and barnyard millet — all equivalent to one shi of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Two shi of millet, panicled millet, broomcorn, barley, buckwheat, or kaoliang would equal one shi of rice; two and a half shi of husked rice, sorghum, or glutinous millet; three shi of coix or barnyard millet — each equivalent to one shi of rice.

sentences.zh: 小麥芝麻豆與米等。

translations.literal: Wheat, sesame, and beans were equivalent to rice.
translations.idiomatic: Wheat, sesame, and beans counted one-for-one with rice.

sentences.zh: 」從之，著為令。

translations.literal: [The proposal] was approved and promulgated as an ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved and codified as law.

sentences.zh: 又更定屯守之數。

translations.literal: The ratio of farming to garrison duty was also revised.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison-to-farming ratios were also revised.

sentences.zh: 臨邊險要，守多於屯。

translations.literal: Where the frontier was strategically critical, garrison exceeded farming.
translations.idiomatic: At the most strategic frontier points, garrison duty outweighed farming.

sentences.zh: 地僻處及輸糧艱者，屯多於守，屯兵百名委百戶，三百名委千戶，五百名以上指揮提督之。

translations.literal: In remote areas and where transporting grain was difficult, farming exceeded garrison duty; colonists numbering one hundred were placed under a centurion, three hundred under a chiliarch, five hundred or more under a commander as supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: In remote or supply-starved regions, farming took priority; units of 100 colonists reported to a centurion, 300 to a chiliarch, and 500 or more to a battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 屯設紅牌，列則例於上。

translations.literal: At each colony a red placard was posted listing the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Each colony posted a red placard listing the rules.

sentences.zh: 年六十與殘疾及幼者，耕以自食，不限於例。

translations.literal: Those aged sixty, the disabled, and the young farmed for their own subsistence, not bound by the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers over sixty, the disabled, and minors farmed for their own subsistence outside the quota system.

sentences.zh: 屯軍以公事妨農務者，免徵子粒，且禁衛所差撥。

translations.literal: Colony soldiers whose official duties interfered with farm work were exempted from grain levies, and guard units were forbidden to reassign them.
translations.idiomatic: Colonists pulled from farming by official duties were exempt from grain levies, and guard units were barred from reassigning them arbitrarily.

sentences.zh: 於時，東自遼左，北抵宣、大，西至甘肅，南盡滇、蜀，極於交阯，中原則大河南北，在在興屯矣。

translations.literal: At that time, from Liaodong in the east, north to Xuanfu and Datong, west to Gansu, south to Yunnan and Sichuan, extending to Jiaozhi, and in the Central Plains north and south of the Yellow River — colonies were flourishing everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Colonies sprang up everywhere — from Liaodong in the east to Xuanfu and Datong in the north, Gansu in the west, Yunnan and Sichuan in the south, even Jiaozhi; throughout the Yellow River heartland, garrison farming was universal.

sentences.zh: 宣宗之世，屢核各屯，以征戍罷耕及官豪勢要佔匿者，減餘糧之半。

translations.literal: During the Xuande reign, colonies were repeatedly audited; for those who neglected farming due to campaigns and garrison duty, and for powerful officials who occupied and concealed [land], half the surplus grain quota was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Xuande Emperor, repeated colony audits penalized units that abandoned farming for campaigns and powerful families that seized colony land — cutting their surplus-grain quota by half.

sentences.zh: 迤北來歸就屯之人，給車牛農器。

translations.literal: People coming from the north to join colonies were given carts, oxen, and farm implements.
translations.idiomatic: Settlers arriving from the northern steppe received carts, oxen, and farm tools.

sentences.zh: 分遼東各衛屯軍為三等，丁牛兼者為上，丁牛有一為中，俱無者為下。

translations.literal: Colony soldiers in the various Liaodong guards were divided into three grades: those with both labor and oxen were upper grade; those with one of the two were middle grade; those with neither were lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong colony troops were classified in three tiers: those with both manpower and oxen ranked highest; those with one or the other, middle; those with neither, lowest.

sentences.zh: 英宗免軍田正糧歸倉，止徵餘糧六石。

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong exempted standard grain on military colony fields from returning to the granary, collecting only six shi of surplus grain.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong exempted the twelve-shi subsistence quota from granary collection, taxing only six shi of surplus.

sentences.zh: 後又免沿邊開田官軍子粒，減各邊屯田子粒有差。

translations.literal: Later, grain levies on frontier colonists opening new fields were also exempted, and colony grain levies on various frontiers were reduced by differing amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Later, frontier colonists who opened new land were exempted from grain levies, and colony taxes along the borders were reduced by varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 景帝時，邊方多事，令兵分為兩番，六日操守，六日耕種。

translations.literal: During the Jingdi reign, the frontier saw many disturbances; troops were divided into two shifts — six days on garrison duty, six days farming.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jingtai Emperor, with the frontier in turmoil, troops were split into two rotations — six days on guard, six days farming.

sentences.zh: 成化初，宣府巡撫葉盛買官牛千八百，並置農具，遣軍屯田，收糧易銀，以補官馬耗損，邊入稱便。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua, Xuanfu Grand Coordinator Ye Sheng purchased 1,800 government oxen and also provided farm tools, dispatching soldiers to colony farm; grain collected was exchanged for silver to cover official horse losses — frontier inhabitants praised the convenience.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Chenghua reign, Xuanfu coordinator Ye Sheng bought 1,800 government oxen, supplied tools, and put troops to farming; grain was sold for silver to cover cavalry horse losses — to general approval on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 自正統後，屯政稍弛，而屯糧猶存三之二。

translations.literal: After the Zhengtong reign, colony administration gradually slackened, yet colony grain still remained two-thirds [of the original amount].
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhengtong era, colony administration slackened, but colony grain revenues still stood at about two-thirds of their peak.

sentences.zh: 其後屯田多為內監、軍官佔奪，法盡壞。

translations.literal: Thereafter colony fields were largely seized by eunuchs and military officers; the system was completely ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Colony land was soon seized by eunuchs and military officers, and the system collapsed entirely.

sentences.zh: 憲宗之世頗議釐復，而視舊所入，不能什一矣。

translations.literal: During the Xianzong reign there was considerable discussion of restoration, but compared with old revenue, [recovery] could not reach one-tenth.
translations.idiomatic: The Chenghua court debated restoration, but recovered revenues amounted to less than a tenth of the original intake.

sentences.zh: 弘治間，屯糧愈輕，有畝止三升者。

translations.literal: During Hongzhi, colony grain grew ever lighter; in some cases only three sheng per mu.
translations.idiomatic: By the Hongzhi era, colony yields had shrunk so far that some plots yielded only three sheng per mu.

sentences.zh: 沿及正德，遼東屯田較永樂間田贏萬八千餘頃，而糧乃縮四萬六千餘石。

translations.literal: Extending into Zhengde, Liaodong colony fields exceeded those of the Yongle era by more than eighteen thousand qing, yet grain [collection] shrank by more than forty-six thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: By the Zhengde era, Liaodong registered 18,000 more qing than under Yongle — yet grain collections had fallen by over 46,000 shi.

sentences.zh: 初，永樂時，屯田米常溢三之一，常操軍十九萬，以屯軍四萬供之。

translations.literal: Initially, during Yongle, colony rice often exceeded [needs] by one-third; the standing garrison numbered 190,000, supplied by 40,000 colony soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle's day, colony grain regularly ran one-third over quota; 40,000 colonists fed a standing force of 190,000.

sentences.zh: 而受供者又得自耕。

translations.literal: And those receiving provisions could also farm for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Those receiving rations could also farm on their own account.

sentences.zh: 邊外軍無月糧，以是邊餉恆足。

translations.literal: Frontier troops beyond the passes received no monthly rations; thus frontier supplies were always sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Troops beyond the passes had no monthly stipend, yet frontier provisions remained ample — thanks to colony grain.

sentences.zh: 及是，屯軍多逃死，常操軍止八萬，皆仰給於倉。

translations.literal: By this time, many colony soldiers had fled or died; the standing garrison numbered only 80,000, all dependent on granary supplies.
translations.idiomatic: By now most colonists had fled or died; the standing force had fallen to 80,000, entirely dependent on government stores.

sentences.zh: 而邊外數擾，棄不耕。

translations.literal: Meanwhile, the outer frontier was repeatedly disturbed, and [land] was abandoned and left uncultivated.
translations.idiomatic: The outer frontier, repeatedly raided, lay fallow.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾擅政，遣官分出丈田責逋。

translations.literal: When Liu Jin wielded power, officials were dispatched to survey fields and collect arrears.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jin seized power, he sent officials to survey land and collect tax arrears.

sentences.zh: 希瑾意者，偽增田數，蒐括慘毒，戶部侍郎韓福尤急刻。

translations.literal: Those seeking to please Jin fraudulently inflated field counts and extorted with cruel severity; Vice Minister of Revenue Han Fu was especially harsh and grasping.
translations.idiomatic: Officials currying favor with Jin inflated land figures and extorted with brutal zeal; Vice Minister Han Fu was the most ruthless of all.

sentences.zh: 遼卒不堪，脅眾為亂，撫之乃定。

translations.literal: Liaodong soldiers could not bear it; they coerced the masses into rebellion; [the disturbance] was pacified only after soothing measures.
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong soldiers, driven past endurance, rose in mutiny; the disturbance was quelled only after concessions from the authorities.

sentences.zh: 明初，募鹽商於各邊開中，謂之商屯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Ming, salt merchants were recruited at each frontier to open transport stations, and this was called merchant colonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Ming, the court recruited salt merchants to establish transport stations along the frontiers—a system known as merchant colonies.

sentences.zh: 迨弘治中，葉淇變法，而開中始壞。

translations.literal: By the Hongzhi era, Ye Qi reformed the law, and the transport-station system began to collapse.
translations.idiomatic: By the Hongzhi reign, Ye Qi's reforms had broken the transport-station system.

sentences.zh: 諸淮商悉撤業歸，西北商亦多徙家於淮，邊地為墟，米石直銀五兩，而邊儲枵然矣。

translations.literal: All Huai salt merchants completely withdrew their business and returned home; northwestern merchants also mostly moved their families to the Huai region; frontier lands became wasteland; a shi of rice was worth five taels of silver, and frontier reserves were empty.
translations.idiomatic: Huai salt merchants quit the trade entirely; northwestern merchants likewise relocated their households to the Huai region; frontier districts turned to ruins; rice reached five taels per shi, and border granaries stood empty.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，楊一清復請召商開中，又請仿古募民實塞下之意，招徠隴右、關西民以屯邊。

translations.literal: During the Shizong reign, Yang Yiqing again requested summoning merchants to open transport stations, and also requested following the ancient meaning of recruiting commoners to settle the frontier, to attract people from Longyou and western Guanzhong to colonize the border.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jiajing emperor, Yang Yiqing renewed the call for merchant transport stations and proposed reviving the old policy of settling civilians on the frontier, recruiting people from Longyou and western Guanzhong to garrison the border.

sentences.zh: 其後周澤、王崇古、林富、陳世輔、王畿、王朝用、唐順之、吳桂芳等爭言屯政。

translations.literal: Subsequently Zhou Ze, Wang Chonggu, Lin Fu, Chen Shifu, Wang Ji, Wang Chaoyong, Tang Shunzhi, Wu Guifang, and others all competed to speak on colony policy.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Zhou Ze, Wang Chonggu, Lin Fu, Chen Shifu, Wang Ji, Wang Chaoyong, Tang Shunzhi, Wu Guifang, and others all pressed proposals for colony administration.

sentences.zh: 而龐尚鵬總理江北鹽屯，尋移九邊，與總督王崇古，先後區畫屯政甚詳。

translations.literal: Pang Shangpeng took charge of salt colonies in Jiangbei, then soon transferred to the Nine Frontiers, and together with Governor-General Wang Chonggu, successively planned colony policy in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Shangpeng oversaw salt colonies in Jiangbei, then moved on to the Nine Frontiers, where he and Governor-General Wang Chonggu worked out colony policy in painstaking detail.

sentences.zh: 然是時因循日久，卒鮮實效。

translations.literal: But at that time procrastination had lasted long, and in the end there was little actual effect.
translations.idiomatic: By then inertia had set in for years, and in the end little was actually achieved.

sentences.zh: 給事中管懷理言：「屯田不興，其弊有四：疆埸戒嚴，一也；

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Guan Huaili said: "Colony fields do not flourish; its ills are four: frontier vigilance is strict, the first;"
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Guan Huaili said: "Colony farming cannot thrive. There are four reasons: first, the frontier is under strict military alert;"

sentences.zh: 牛種不給，二也；

translations.literal: Oxen and seed are not supplied, the second;
translations.idiomatic: second, oxen and seed are not provided;

sentences.zh: 丁壯亡徙，三也；

translations.literal: Able-bodied men flee and migrate, the third;
translations.idiomatic: third, able-bodied men flee and disperse;

sentences.zh: 田在敵外，四也。

translations.literal: Fields lie beyond enemy territory, the fourth.
translations.idiomatic: fourth, the fields lie beyond enemy lines;

sentences.zh: 如是而管屯者猶欲按籍增賦，非扣月糧，即按丁賠補耳。」

translations.literal: Yet despite this, those managing colonies still wish to increase levies according to registers—either deducting monthly rations or assessing per capita compensation."
translations.idiomatic: Even so, colony administrators still try to raise assessments from the registers—either by docking monthly rations or by charging per capita make-up payments."

sentences.zh: 屯糧之輕，至弘、正而極，嘉靖中漸增，隆慶間復畝收一斗。

translations.literal: The lightness of colony grain reached its extreme in the Hongzhi and Zhengde reigns; in Jiajing it gradually increased, and during Longqing it returned to one dou per mu.
translations.idiomatic: Colony yields hit their lowest point under Hongzhi and Zhengde; they rose again in Jiajing, and by Longqing the levy had returned to one dou per mu.

sentences.zh: 然屯丁逃亡者益多。

translations.literal: Yet colony draftees fleeing grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Yet more and more colonists deserted their posts.

sentences.zh: 管糧郎中不問屯田有無，月糧止半給。

translations.literal: The grain officials paid no heed to whether colony fields existed, issuing only half the monthly rations.
translations.idiomatic: Grain officials paid no attention to whether colony fields were actually farmed and issued only half the monthly rations.

sentences.zh: 沿邊屯地，或變為斥鹵、沙磧，糧額不得減。
