translations.literal: Frontier colony lands sometimes turned saline or sandy, yet the grain quota could not be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier colony plots sometimes turned saline or sandy, yet the grain quota could not be lowered.

sentences.zh: 屯田御史又於額外增本折，屯軍益不堪命。

translations.literal: The colony-field censor further added capital conversion beyond the quota, and colony troops could bear it less and less.
translations.idiomatic: The colony-field censor added extra capital conversion charges on top of the quota, and colonists found the burden increasingly unbearable.

sentences.zh: 萬歷時，計屯田之數六十四萬四千餘頃，視洪武時虧二十四萬九千餘頃，田日減而糧日增，其弊如此。

translations.literal: In the Wanli era, colony fields totaled more than 644,000 qing—a loss of more than 249,000 qing compared with Hongwu—fields dwindling daily while grain assessments rose; such were the ills.
translations.idiomatic: By the Wanli era, registered colony land stood at more than 644,000 qing—249,000 qing less than under Hongwu. Fields shrank year by year while grain quotas grew; such was the decay.

sentences.zh: 時則山東巡撫鄭汝璧請開登州海北長山諸島田。

translations.literal: At that time Shandong governor Zheng Rubi requested opening fields on the Changshan islands north of the sea at Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, Shandong governor Zheng Rubi proposed opening farmland on the Changshan islands off the north coast of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 福建巡撫許孚遠墾閩海壇山田成，復請開南日山、澎湖；

translations.literal: Fujian governor Xu Fuyuan successfully reclaimed fields on Tanshan along the Fujian coast and further requested opening lands on Nanri Mountain and Penghu;
translations.idiomatic: Fujian governor Xu Fuyuan successfully reclaimed fields on Tanshan along the Fujian coast and then requested opening land on Nanri Mountain and Penghu as well;

sentences.zh: 又言浙江濱海諸山，若陳錢、金塘、補陀、玉環、南麂，皆可經理。

translations.literal: He also stated that coastal mountains in Zhejiang—Chenqian, Jintang, Putuo, Yuhuan, and Nanji—could all be developed.
translations.idiomatic: he also argued that coastal hills in Zhejiang—Chenqian, Jintang, Putuo, Yuhuan, and Nanji—could all be brought under cultivation.

sentences.zh: 天津巡撫汪應蛟則請於天津興屯。

translations.literal: Tianjin governor Wang Yingjiao requested establishing colonies at Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjin governor Wang Yingjiao, for his part, proposed establishing colonies at Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 或留中不下，或不久輒廢。

translations.literal: Some proposals were held at court and never issued; others were abandoned shortly after implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Some plans were shelved at court and never enacted; others were abandoned soon after they began.

sentences.zh: 熹宗之世，巡按張慎言復議天津屯田。

translations.literal: Under the Tianqi emperor, touring censor Zhang Shenyan again proposed Tianjin colony fields.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tianqi emperor, touring censor Zhang Shenyan revived the proposal for Tianjin colony farming.

sentences.zh: 而御史左光鬥命管河通判盧觀象大興水田之利，太常少卿董應舉踵而行之。

translations.literal: Censor Zuo Guangdou ordered river commissioner Lu Guanxiang to develop paddy fields extensively, and Vice Minister of Imperial Rites Dong Yingju followed in his footsteps.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zuo Guangdou ordered river commissioner Lu Guanxiang to expand paddy cultivation on a large scale, and Vice Minister of Imperial Rites Dong Yingju took up the work in turn.

sentences.zh: 光鬥更於河間、天津設屯學，試騎射，為武生給田百畝。

translations.literal: Zuo further established colony schools in Hejian and Tianjin, testing mounted archery and granting military students one hundred mu each.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo also set up colony schools in Hejian and Tianjin, tested candidates in horsemanship and archery, and granted one hundred mu to each student who passed.

sentences.zh: 李繼貞巡撫天津，亦力於屯務，然仍歲旱蝗，弗克底成效也。

translations.literal: Li Jizhen, governor of Tianjin, also pursued colony work vigorously, but drought and locusts struck year after year, so no lasting results could be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jizhen, governor of Tianjin, also threw himself into colony work, but drought and locusts came year after year, and nothing lasting could be achieved.

sentences.zh: 明時，草場頗多，佔奪民業。

translations.literal: During the Ming there were many pasture grounds, and they encroached on commoners' holdings.
translations.idiomatic: In the Ming there were many pasture grounds, and they often encroached on private holdings.

sentences.zh: 而為民厲者，莫如皇莊及諸王、勳戚、中官莊田為甚。

translations.literal: Yet none brought more harm to the people than imperial estates and the manor lands of princes, meritorious kin, and eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: But nothing harmed the people more than imperial estates and the manor lands of princes, meritorious kin, and eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 太祖賜勳臣公侯丞相以下莊田，多者百頃，親王莊田千頃。

translations.literal: The Founder granted manor lands to meritorious officials from duke and marquis down to grand councillors—up to one hundred qing in the largest cases; princes received one thousand qing.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwu emperor granted manor lands to meritorious officials from dukes and marquises down to grand councillors—up to one hundred qing in the largest cases—and princes received one thousand qing.

sentences.zh: 又賜公侯暨武臣公田，又賜百官公田，以其租入充祿。

translations.literal: He also granted public fields to dukes, marquises, and military officers, and public fields to civil officials, using the rent as salary.
translations.idiomatic: He also granted public fields to dukes, marquises, and military officers, and public fields to civil officials as well, using the rent to pay their salaries.

sentences.zh: 指揮沒於陣者皆賜公田。

translations.literal: Commanders who died in battle all received public fields.
translations.idiomatic: Every commander who fell in battle was granted public fields.

sentences.zh: 勳臣莊佃，多倚威捍禁，帝召諸臣戒諭之。

translations.literal: Tenants on meritorious officials' manors often relied on their patrons' power to resist restrictions; the emperor summoned the ministers and admonished them.
translations.idiomatic: Tenants on the manors of meritorious officials often used their patrons' power to defy the law; the emperor summoned the ministers and warned them against it.

sentences.zh: 其後公侯復歲祿，歸賜田於官。

translations.literal: Later dukes and marquises received annual stipends again and returned the granted fields to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Later dukes and marquises were restored to annual stipends and returned their granted fields to the state.

sentences.zh: 仁、宣之世，乞請漸廣，大臣亦得請沒官莊舍。

translations.literal: In the Ren-Xuan era, petitions gradually expanded, and grand ministers could also request confiscated manor houses and land.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Hongxi and Xuande emperors, land petitions grew more common, and even grand ministers could request confiscated manor houses and estates.

sentences.zh: 然甯王權請灌城為庶子耕牧地，帝賜書，援祖制拒之。

translations.literal: But Prince Ning Quan requested Guancheng as farmland and pasture for lesser sons; the emperor sent a letter citing ancestral precedent to refuse.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ning Quan asked for Guancheng as farmland and pasture for his younger sons, the emperor replied in writing, citing ancestral precedent to refuse.

sentences.zh: 至英宗時，諸王、外戚、中官所在佔官私田，或反誣民佔，請案治。

translations.literal: By the Yingzong era, princes, in-laws, and eunuchs seized official and private lands everywhere, sometimes falsely accusing commoners of encroachment and demanding prosecution.
translations.idiomatic: By the reign of Emperor Yingzong, princes, imperial in-laws, and eunuchs were seizing official and private land everywhere, sometimes falsely accusing commoners of encroachment and demanding prosecution.

sentences.zh: 比案問得實，帝命還之民者非一。

translations.literal: When investigations proved the truth, the emperor ordered restitution to commoners in not a few cases.
translations.idiomatic: When investigations proved the facts, the emperor ordered land returned to the people in more than one case.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔禁奪民田及奏請畿內地。

translations.literal: He then issued an edict forbidding seizure of commoners' land and petitioning for land within the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: He then issued an edict forbidding the seizure of commoners' land and petitions for land within the capital region.

sentences.zh: 然權貴宗室莊田墳塋，或賜或請，不可勝計。

translations.literal: Yet manor lands and tombs of the powerful and imperial clan, whether granted or petitioned for, were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Yet manor lands and burial grounds for the powerful and the imperial clan, whether granted or petitioned for, were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 御馬太監劉順家人進薊州草場，進獻由此始。

translations.literal: Imperial horse supervisor Liu Shun's household presented the Jizhou pasture grounds—thus began the practice of presenting land.
translations.idiomatic: The household of Imperial Horse Supervisor Liu Shun presented the Jizhou pasture grounds to the throne—and with that began the practice of land presentations.

sentences.zh: 宦官之田，則自尹奉、喜寧始。

translations.literal: Eunuch landholdings began with Yin Feng and Xi Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch landholdings began with Yin Feng and Xi Ning.

sentences.zh: 初，洪熙時，有仁壽宮莊，其後又有清寧、未央宮莊。

translations.literal: Initially during Hongxi there was the Renshou Palace estate; later there were also Qingning and Weiyang Palace estates.
translations.idiomatic: At first, under Hongxi, there was the Renshou Palace estate; later came the Qingning and Weiyang Palace estates as well.

sentences.zh: 天順三年，以諸王未出閣，供用浩繁，立東宮、德王、秀王莊田。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianshun, because princes had not yet left the palace, expenses were enormous, and estates were established for the crown prince, Prince De, and Prince Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianshun, because the princes had not yet left the palace and expenses were heavy, estates were set up for the crown prince, Prince De, and Prince Xiu.

sentences.zh: 二王之籓，地仍歸官。

translations.literal: When the two princes went to their fiefs, the land reverted to the state.
translations.idiomatic: When the two princes went to their fiefs, the land reverted to the state.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，以沒入曹吉祥地為宮中莊田，皇莊之名由此始。

translations.literal: When Xianzong ascended, he confiscated Cao Jixiang's lands as palace estates—the name "imperial estate" began here.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne, he confiscated Cao Jixiang's lands as palace estates—the term "imperial estate" dates from this.

sentences.zh: 其後莊田遍郡縣。

translations.literal: Afterward manor lands spread throughout counties and prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After that, manor lands spread through counties and prefectures everywhere.

sentences.zh: 給事中齊莊言：「天子以四海為家，何必置立莊田，與貧民較利。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Qi Zhuang said: "The Son of Heaven takes the four seas as his home—why must he establish manor lands and compete for profit with the poor?"
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Qi Zhuang said: "The Son of Heaven takes the four seas as his home—why establish manor lands and compete for profit with the poor?"

sentences.zh: 」弗聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 弘治二年，戶部尚書李敏等以災異上言：「畿內皇莊有五，共地萬二千八百餘頃；

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongzhi, Minister of Revenue Li Min and others memorialized on calamities: "Within the capital region there are five imperial estates, totaling more than 12,800 qing;"
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Hongzhi, Minister of Revenue Li Min and others memorialized on calamities: "Within the capital region there are five imperial estates, totaling more than 12,800 qing;"

sentences.zh: 勳戚、中官莊田三百三十有二，共地三萬三千餘頃。

translations.literal: Meritorious kin and eunuch estates number 332, totaling more than 33,000 qing.
translations.idiomatic: there are 332 estates belonging to meritorious kin and eunuchs, totaling more than 33,000 qing.

sentences.zh: 管莊官校招集羣小，稱莊頭、伴當，佔地土，斂財物，汙婦女。

translations.literal: Estate managers gather hoodlums called estate heads and attendants—they seize land, extort goods, and violate women.
translations.idiomatic: Estate managers recruit thugs called estate heads and attendants—they seize land, extort goods, and assault women.

sentences.zh: 稍與分辯，輒被誣奏。

translations.literal: Slight resistance brings false accusations to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who so much as disputes them is falsely accused to the throne.

sentences.zh: 官校執縛，舉家驚惶。

translations.literal: Official agents arrest and bind them; whole families are terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Official agents arrest and bind them, and whole families are thrown into terror.

sentences.zh: 民心傷痛入骨，災異所由生。

translations.literal: Popular resentment runs bone-deep—the source of calamities.
translations.idiomatic: Popular grief runs bone-deep; this is where calamities come from.

sentences.zh: 乞革去管莊之人，付小民耕種，畝徵銀三分，充各宮用度。

translations.literal: I beg to abolish estate managers, let commoners farm, and levy three fen of silver per mu for palace expenses.
translations.idiomatic: We beg that estate managers be removed, the land turned over to commoners to farm, and three fen of silver levied per mu to meet the needs of the palaces.

sentences.zh: 」帝命戒飭莊戶。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the estate households admonished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the estate households admonished.

sentences.zh: 又因御史言，罷仁壽宮莊，還之草場，且命凡侵牧地者，悉還其舊。

translations.literal: Following censor memorials, the Renshou Palace estate was abolished and returned to pasture; all who had encroached on grazing land must restore it.
translations.idiomatic: On the censors' advice, the Renshou Palace estate was abolished and returned to pasture, and anyone who had encroached on grazing land was ordered to restore it.

sentences.zh: 又定制，獻地王府者戍邊。

translations.literal: A regulation was also made: those who presented land to princely residences would be sent to frontier garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: A regulation was also issued: anyone who presented land to a princely residence would be sent to frontier garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 奉禦趙瑄獻雄縣地為皇莊，戶部尚書周經劾其違制，下瑄詔獄。

translations.literal: Palace attendant Zhao Xuan presented Xiong County land as an imperial estate; Minister of Revenue Zhou Jing impeached him for violating regulations, and Zhao was imprisoned by imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant Zhao Xuan presented Xiong County land as an imperial estate; Minister of Revenue Zhou Jing impeached him for violating regulations, and Zhao was imprisoned by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 敕諸王輔導官，導王奏請者罪之。

translations.literal: An edict directed princes' tutors: any who guided princes in such petitions would be punished.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed the tutors of the princes: any who guided a prince in such petitions would be punished.

sentences.zh: 然當日奏獻不絕，氣請亦愈繁。

translations.literal: Yet presentations continued unabated that day, and bold petitions grew ever more frequent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet land presentations never stopped, and shameless petitions grew ever bolder.

sentences.zh: 徽、興、岐、衡四王，田多至七千餘頃。

translations.literal: The four princes Hui, Xing, Qi, and Heng held up to more than 7,000 qing each.
translations.idiomatic: The four princes Hui, Xing, Qi, and Heng each held as much as seven thousand qing or more.

sentences.zh: 會昌、建昌、慶雲三侯爭田，帝輒賜之。

translations.literal: The three marquises Huichang, Jianchang, and Qingyun disputed land; the emperor promptly granted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the three marquises Huichang, Jianchang, and Qingyun disputed land, the emperor promptly granted it to them.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，逾月即建皇莊七，其後增至三百餘處。

translations.literal: When Wuzong ascended, within a month he established seven imperial estates; they later grew to more than three hundred locations.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong took the throne, he established seven imperial estates within a month; they later grew to more than three hundred.

sentences.zh: 諸王、外戚求請及奪民田者無算。

translations.literal: Princes, in-laws, petitions, and seizures of commoners' land were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and imperial in-laws petitioned for land and seized commoners' fields beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，命給事中夏言等清核皇莊田。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign, he ordered Supervising Secretaries Xia Yan and others to audit and verify imperial estate lands.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign, the emperor ordered Supervising Secretaries Xia Yan and others to audit imperial estate lands.

sentences.zh: 言極言皇莊為厲於民。

translations.literal: Yan spoke forcefully that imperial estates were a scourge to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yan spoke forcefully of the harm imperial estates did to the people.

sentences.zh: 自是正德以來投獻侵牟之地，頗有給還民者，而宦戚輩復中撓之。

translations.literal: From then on, lands presented and encroached upon since Zhengde were in many cases returned to the people, but eunuchs and in-laws again obstructed from within.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, much of the land presented and seized since the Zhengde era was returned to the people, but eunuchs and imperial in-laws again sabotaged the effort from within.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書孫交造皇莊新冊，額減於舊。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Sun Jiao compiled a new register of imperial estates, with totals reduced from the old.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue Sun Jiao compiled a new register of imperial estates, with totals lower than before.

sentences.zh: 帝命核先年頃畝數以聞，改稱官地，不復名皇莊，詔所司徵銀解部。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered verification of acreage from previous years to be reported, renamed them official lands, no longer called imperial estates, and decreed that the responsible offices collect silver and remit it to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered a verification of acreage from previous years, renamed the lands official property rather than imperial estates, and decreed that the responsible offices collect silver and remit it to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 然多為宦寺中飽，積逋至數十萬以為常。

translations.literal: Yet much was embezzled by eunuchs; arrears of hundreds of thousands became the norm.
translations.idiomatic: Yet eunuchs embezzled much of it, and arrears in the hundreds of thousands became routine.

sentences.zh: 是時，禁勳戚奏討、奸民投獻者，又革王府所請山場湖陂。

translations.literal: At that time, petitions by meritorious kin and illegal presentations by scheming commoners were forbidden, and princely requests for hills, lakes, and ponds were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, petitions from meritorious kin and illegal land presentations by schemers were banned, and princely requests for hills, lakes, and ponds were abolished.

sentences.zh: 德王請齊、漢二庶人所遺東昌、兗州閒田，又請白雲等湖，山東巡撫邵錫按新令卻之，語甚切。

translations.literal: Prince De requested the abandoned lands left by the two junior princes Qi and Han in Dongchang and Yanzhou, and also requested lakes such as Baiyun; Shandong governor Shao Xi rejected this according to the new regulations, his language very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Prince De requested the abandoned lands in Dongchang and Yanzhou left by the two junior princes Qi and Han, and also asked for lakes such as Baiyun; Shandong governor Shao Xi rejected the requests under the new rules in sharply worded terms.

sentences.zh: 德王爭之數四，帝仍從部議，但存籓封初請莊田。

translations.literal: Prince De disputed four times; the emperor still followed the ministry's counsel, retaining only the manor lands initially requested at enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Prince De disputed the matter four times, but the emperor still sided with the ministry, allowing only the manor lands originally granted at enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 其後有奏請者不聽。

translations.literal: Afterward, petitions were not approved.
translations.idiomatic: After that, further petitions were not approved.

sentences.zh: 又定，凡公主、國公莊田，世遠者存什三。

translations.literal: It was also fixed that for princess and state-duke manor lands, after many generations only three-tenths would remain.
translations.idiomatic: It was also decreed that for princess and state-duke manor lands, after many generations only three-tenths would be retained.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十九年遣御史瀋陽清奪隱冒莊田萬六千餘頃。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year of Jiajing, Censor Shen Yang was dispatched to clear more than 16,000 qing of concealed and falsely registered manor lands.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year of Jiajing, Censor Shen Yang was dispatched to recover more than 16,000 qing of concealed and falsely registered manor lands.

sentences.zh: 穆宗從御史王廷瞻言，復定世次遞減之限：勳臣五世限田二百頃，戚畹七百頃至七十頃有差。

translations.literal: Muzong followed Censor Wang Tingzhan's advice and re-established generational reduction limits: meritorious officials in the fifth generation were limited to 200 qing; imperial in-laws from 700 qing down to 70 qing by rank.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong followed Censor Wang Tingzhan's advice and re-established generational reduction limits: meritorious officials in the fifth generation were capped at 200 qing; imperial in-laws from 700 qing down to 70 qing depending on rank.

sentences.zh: 初，世宗時，承天六莊二湖地八千三百餘頃，領以中官，又聽校舍兼併，增八百八十頃，分為十二莊。

translations.literal: Initially during Shizong's reign, Chengtian had six estates and two lakes totaling more than 8,300 qing, overseen by eunuchs; schools were also allowed to annex land, adding 880 qing, divided into twelve estates.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jiajing emperor, Chengtian had six estates and two lakes totaling more than 8,300 qing, overseen by eunuchs; schools were also allowed to annex land, adding 880 qing and splitting the holdings into twelve estates.

sentences.zh: 至是始領之有司，兼併者還民。

translations.literal: At this point oversight passed to regular officials, and annexed lands were returned to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Now oversight passed to regular officials, and annexed lands were returned to the people.

sentences.zh: 又著令宗室買田不輸役者沒官，皇親田俱令有司徵之，如勳臣例。

translations.literal: It was also ordered that imperial clan members who bought land but evaded corvée labor would have it confiscated, and all imperial kin lands would be collected by regular officials according to the meritorious-official precedent.
translations.idiomatic: It was also decreed that any imperial clansman who bought land but evaded corvée labor would have it confiscated, and all imperial kin lands would be collected by regular officials on the same terms as meritorious officials.

sentences.zh: 雖請乞不乏，而賜額有定，徵收有制，民害少衰止。

translations.literal: Although petitions never ceased, grants had fixed limits and collection had regulations, and harm to the people abated somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Although petitions never ceased, grants had fixed limits and collection followed rules, and the harm to the people eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 神宗賚予過侈，求無不獲。

translations.literal: Shenzong's grants and bestowals were excessively lavish; requests were never denied.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong's grants were extravagantly generous; no request went unfulfilled.

sentences.zh: 潞王、壽陽公主恩最渥。

translations.literal: Prince Lu and Princess Shouyang received the greatest favor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lu and Princess Shouyang received the greatest favor.

sentences.zh: 而福王分封，括河南、山東、湖廣田為王莊，至四萬頃。

translations.literal: When Prince Fu was enfeoffed, lands in Henan, Shandong, and Huguang were seized for princely estates, reaching 40,000 qing.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Fu was enfeoffed, land across Henan, Shandong, and Huguang was seized for princely estates, reaching forty thousand qing.

sentences.zh: 羣臣力爭，乃減其半。

translations.literal: Ministers protested vigorously, and the amount was halved.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers protested vigorously, and the grant was cut in half.

sentences.zh: 王府官及諸閹丈地徵稅，旁午於道，扈養廝役廩食以萬計，漁斂慘毒不忍聞。

translations.literal: Princely officials and eunuchs measured land and collected taxes continuously on the roads; retainers and servants numbered in the tens of thousands; extortion was brutally cruel beyond bearing to hear.
translations.idiomatic: Princely officials and eunuchs measured land and collected taxes in an unending stream along the roads; retainers and servants numbered in the tens of thousands, and their extortion was so brutally cruel it was unbearable to hear.

sentences.zh: 駕帖捕民，格殺莊佃，所在騷然。

translations.literal: Imperial warrants arrested commoners and killed estate tenants; turmoil erupted everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial warrants were used to arrest commoners and kill estate tenants, and unrest broke out everywhere.

sentences.zh: 給事中官應震、姚宗文等屢疏諫，皆不報。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Guan Yingzhen, Yao Zongwen, and others repeatedly memorialized in remonstrance, but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretaries Guan Yingzhen, Yao Zongwen, and others memorialized repeatedly in protest, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 時復更定勳戚莊田世次遞減法，視舊制稍寬。

translations.literal: At the time the generational reduction law for meritorious kin manor lands was revised again, somewhat looser than the old system.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the generational reduction rules for meritorious kin manor lands were revised again, somewhat more lenient than before.

sentences.zh: 其後應議減者，輒奉詔姑留，不能革也。

translations.literal: Afterward, whenever reduction was debated, imperial edicts usually deferred abolition; reform could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, whenever reduction was debated, an edict would usually defer abolition—reform could never be carried through.

sentences.zh: 熹宗時，桂、惠、瑞三王及遂平、甯德二公主莊田，動以萬計，而魏忠賢一門，橫賜尤甚。

translations.literal: Under Tianqi, the three princes Gui, Hui, and Rui and the two princesses Suiping and Ningde held manor lands reckoned in the tens of thousands of qing; the clan of Wei Zhongxian received especially extravagant grants.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tianqi emperor, the three princes Gui, Hui, and Rui and the two princesses Suiping and Ningde held manor lands reckoned in the tens of thousands of qing, while the clan of Wei Zhongxian received especially lavish grants.

sentences.zh: 蓋中葉以後，莊田侵奪民業，與國相終云。

translations.literal: Thus from the mid-dynasty onward, manor lands encroached on commoners' holdings and persisted until the dynasty's end.
translations.idiomatic: From the mid-dynasty onward, manor lands seized commoners' holdings—a scourge that lasted until the dynasty's end.
